description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The path-traced reference crosses a surface that lets light through by its share for its depth along each path, as global illumination's rays cross a canopy, and a note reads the canopy and the voxel game's grove against it.
The scene field holds the meshes drawn into the shadow maps alone as any other, so a cave under rock a game leaves out of its view keeps the sky's light off its floor and a section hidden as the eye crosses stays in the field, item 101's meaning changed by the reviewer's call.
The scene field's pool of triangles holds the build's meshes, each mesh keeps its open edges once found and its parts are cut with a sort by keys, which took the voxel game's frames at their 99th part from 40 ms to 25 as its eye steps across sections at 12 columns.
The suite's runner reads a test ended in under a millisecond as ended and runs again only the tests a lost run left, the Linux job and each of its runs are held to 150 and 90 minutes, and a note names the tests item 131 slowed.
A cell where a second double-sided face of another way passes near, as where two walls cross, keeps its plane too, which the probes' rays read beside the field.
The scene field keeps the plane of the double-sided face nearest each cell, which the probes' rays meet from either side, so two thin walls two cells apart leave the space between them open.
Each screen probe's rays leave from the next place in their texels every frame and the probe keeps up to sixteen frames of its light, so a patch narrower than a texel no longer draws a round spot that stands still.
A resize asked for before the first frame is carried out at once, so a window sized before it draws shows its first frames at that size.
title: 3DEngine
